title: Below zero
goal: I can order negative numbers and add and subtract by jumping along a number line. I can follow a variable that goes below 0 in code.

learn.intro: Numbers below 0 have a minus sign. On a number line, greater numbers are to the right. To add, jump right. To subtract, jump left. When a jump crosses 0, split it at 0. If it does not cross 0, just count the steps.

example.problem: A freezer thermometer reads −8 °C. The door is opened and it rises 5 degrees. Then the door is shut and it falls 9 degrees. What does it read now?
steps: Start at −8. Rising moves right: 5 steps to −3.
Falling moves left. From −3, move 9 steps left to −12. It does not cross 0.

howto.title: How to add and subtract with negative numbers
steps: Mark the start on the number line.
Adding moves right. Subtracting moves left.
If the jump crosses 0, split it at 0. If not, count the steps.
Count the steps in the direction of the jump: never turn round.
Check by jumping back to the start.

try.text: It is −3 °C. It falls 8 degrees. What is the temperature now? {b} °C
try.explanation: Falling moves left. From −3 jump left 8 steps: −3 + (−8) = −11. Check: from −11 jump right 8 to reach −3.

items.text: Put the numbers in order. Begin with the smallest.
items.explanation: The smallest number is the furthest left on the number line: −11, −6, −3, 0, 2, 8. (b) On the number line, the number on the right is greater. −4 is to the right of −10, 0 is right of −2, and −15 is left of 1.

items.text: Read the number line. Each mark is 1 step.

parts.label: b
parts.text: From A to B is {b} steps. From B to C is {b} steps.

items.explanation: A is 1 step right of −10: −9. B is 1 step left of −2: −3. C is 1 step left of 6: 5. From −9 to −3 is 6 steps. From −3 to 5 is 3 + 5 = 8 steps.

items.text: The thermometer shows 3 readings on one day.

parts.label: d
parts.text: From 6 a.m. to noon it rose {b} degrees.

parts.label: e
parts.text: From noon to 9 p.m. it fell {b} degrees.

items.explanation: Read each mark: 6 a.m. is −6 °C, noon is 4 °C and 9 p.m. is −3 °C. From −6 up to 4 is 6 steps to 0 and 4 more: 10 degrees. From 4 down to −3 is 4 steps to 0 and 3 more: 7 degrees.

items.text: Find the value of each one. Use a number line to help.
items.explanation: (a) From −6 jump right 10: 4 steps to 0, then 6 more: 4. (b) From 3 jump left 9: 3 steps to 0, then 6 more: −6. (c) From −7 jump left 5: −12. (d) From −4 jump right 15: 4 steps to 0, then 11 more: 11.

items.text: Find the missing number.
items.explanation: (a) From −5 to 6 is 5 steps to 0 and 6 more: 11. (b) 4 − 7 = −3, so 7. (c) −6 + 8 = 2, so the missing number is −6. (d) −4 − 5 = −9, so the missing number is −4.

items.text: How far is it from the first number to the second? Count the steps, splitting at 0.
items.explanation: (a) From −9 to 4: 9 steps to 0 and 4 more is 13. (b) From −6 to −1: 5 steps, no need to cross 0. (c) From −14 to 31: 14 steps to 0 and 31 more is 45.

items.text: A sprite starts at x = 100. Fill in the blocks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: It ends at x = 0. change x by {b}

parts.label: b
parts.text: With repeat 8 and change x by (−20), it ends at x = {b}.

items.explanation: (a) 4 equal moves must go from 100 down to 0. That is 100 left in 4 moves, so each move is −25. (b) 8 moves of −20 make −160, and 100 − 160 = −60.

items.text: Think about how far each number is from 0.
items.explanation: (a) The distances from 0 are 9, 5, 3, 7 and 4. −3 is only 3 steps from 0. (b) −8 is 8 steps from 0 and 6 is 6 steps from 0, so −8 is further.

items.text: Trace the code. The sprite changes x, then says it.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The last number it says is {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: It says {b} numbers that are below 0.

items.explanation: x starts at 60. Loop 1: 60 − 25 = 35. Loop 2: 10. Loop 3: −15. Loop 4: −40. Loop 5: −65. The 3rd number said is −15. The last is −65. The numbers below 0 are −15, −40 and −65: 3 of them.

items.text: A balance of −15 dollars means Ali owes 15 dollars. Ali has 25 dollars.

parts.label: a
parts.text: He buys a game for 40 dollars. His balance is {b} dollars.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Then he is given 30 dollars. His balance is {b} dollars.

parts.label: c
parts.text: To go from −15 dollars up to 20 dollars, he needs {b} dollars.

items.explanation: (a) 25 − 40 = −15. (b) −15 + 30 = 15. (c) From −15 up to 20: 15 dollars to reach 0, then 20 more, 35 dollars.

items.text: In a card game, scores can go below 0. Ali has −35 points, Ben has 48 points and Cy has −6 points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Ben is {b} points ahead of Ali.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Cy is {b} points ahead of Ali.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Ben wins a round and gets 12 more points. He has {b} points.

items.explanation: (a) From −35 up to 0 is 35, then 48 more: 83 points. (b) From −35 up to −6 is 29 points. (c) 48 + 12 = 60 points.

items.text: To find 6 − (−4), count the steps from −4 up to 6.

parts.label: c
parts.text: So taking away −4 gives the same result as adding {b}.

items.hint: Picture both numbers on a number line.
items.explanation: (a) 6 − (−4): from −4 to 6 is 10 steps. (b) −2 − (−5): from −5 to −2 is 3 steps. (c) In both, subtracting a negative number gave the same answer as adding the matching positive number: 6 + 4 and −2 + 5.

items.text: A sprite starts at x = −90. The loop stops as soon as x is greater than 40 at the start of a repeat.
items.hint: Write x after each repeat. Is it more than 40 yet?
items.explanation: Each repeat changes x by 35 − 10 = 25. After the repeats x is −65, −40, −15, 10, 35, 60. After 5 repeats x = 35, which is not greater than 40, so it repeats a 6th time. It stops with x = 60.

items.text: On Monday at noon it was 3 °C. On Tuesday it was 11 degrees colder than Monday. On Wednesday it was 6 degrees warmer than Tuesday. On Thursday it was −4 °C.

parts.label: c
parts.text: From Monday to Thursday it fell {b} degrees.

items.hint: Draw a number line. Mark Monday first, then each change.
items.explanation: Tuesday: 3 − 11 = −8. Wednesday: −8 + 6 = −2. Thursday is −4, which is 2 below Wednesday. From Monday (3) to Thursday (−4): 3 steps to 0 and 4 more, so it fell 7 degrees.

items.text: Two divers: A is at −12 m and goes down 4 m every minute. B is at −40 m and comes up 6 m every minute.

parts.label: a
parts.text: After 3 minutes, A is at {b} m and B is at {b} m.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B is first above A after minute {b}.

parts.label: c
parts.text: After 5 minutes they are {b} m apart.

items.hint: Make a table: minute, depth of A, depth of B.
items.explanation: After 3 minutes A is at −24 and B at −22, so B is above A (after 2 minutes A −20 and B −28). After 5 minutes A −32 and B −10: 22 m apart.

items.text: This code uses a and b. Run it for each pair of numbers.
items.hint: Is a greater than b? Choose the right branch first.
items.explanation: It says how far apart a and b are. a = −8, b = 5: a is not greater, so 5 − (−8) = 13. a = −3, b = −9: a is greater, so −3 − (−9) = 6. Equal numbers give 0.

items.text: There is no year 0. The year after 1 BC is AD 1. Count the years one by one.

parts.label: a
parts.text: From 5 BC to 1 BC is {b} years.

parts.label: b
parts.text: From 3 BC to AD 4 is {b} years.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A person born in 10 BC dies in AD 12. They are {b} years old.

items.hint: Which year comes straight after 1 BC? Count carefully.
items.explanation: (a) 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 BC: 4 steps. (b) 3 BC, 2 BC, 1 BC, AD 1, 2, 3, 4: 6 steps. (c) 10 BC to 1 BC is 9 steps, 1 more to AD 1, then 11 to AD 12: 21 years.
From −9 jump right 14: 9 steps to 0 and 5 more is 5. From 6 jump left 13: 6 steps to 0 and 7 more is −7.

items.text: Put in order, smallest first:  4, −7, −2, 0  {ll}
items.explanation: On a number line, from left to right: −7, −2, 0, 4.

items.text: It is −6 °C. It rises 11 degrees, then falls 8 degrees. It is now {b} °C.
A sprite starts at x = 20. It runs repeat 3 [change x by −15]. Then x = {b}.
